# About ARC

**The ARC Framework is a technical governance framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating safety and security risks in agentic AI systems.** The framework provides:

- A hierarchical capability taxonomy for classifying agentic system capabilities
- A structured risk mapping distinguishing component, design, and capability-specific risks
- Technical control specifications with risk-to-control mappings
- An implementation methodology for organisational adoption and per-system assessment

New to ARC? Start with [ARC in five minutes](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/in-five-minutes/). What changed in each version of the register is in the [Changelog](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/changelog/).

> **Draft for review**
>
> This site is draft 1 of ARC 2.0 (23 November 2026). It is not the published framework, which is [version 1.3.0](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/agentic-risk-capability-framework/). Please do not cite or adopt it. [How to read and comment on this draft](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft#readme).

> **What's new — register v2.0 (draft)**
>
> Version 2.0 changes the model. An assessment or a contextualised register written against 1.x needs migrating; the [changelog](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/changelog/#v2-0-0) says how.
>
> - **How a capability is used**: each capability that acts on the world is recorded with its [authority, reversibility and reach](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/elements/#context-how-a-capability-is-used), so an assistant that drafts a payment and an agent that pays by itself no longer get the same risks and controls
> - **Protocols** is a fifth component, for connections to tool servers and agents that another party builds or operates; it and Memory are conditional, so their risks apply only to systems that have them
> - **Combination rules** bring a risk into scope whenever a system's capabilities can complete a [dangerous combination](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/capability-combinations/), whichever capabilities supply the parts
> - **Six failure modes**, separating an agent's mistakes from goal-directed misbehaviour, and adding safeguard failure and misuse by the principal
> - **Twelve new risks**, written from a curated file of 366 incidents, covering instruction files, agent credentials, provider dependence, agents that work around their limits, and more
> - **Every control** says where it is enforced, who owns it, what evidence shows it is in place and how to test it, and cites its sources
> - **Overlays** let an organisation keep its own version as one file of changes
> - **Two more crosswalks**: MITRE ATLAS and the Five Eyes guidance on agentic AI

> **Earlier — register v1.3, November 2026**
>
> - **Capability combinations**: a new [page](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/capability-combinations/) on risks that arise only when capabilities are held together, with a check that reads a system's capabilities and reports whether the lethal trifecta (untrusted content, sensitive data, and an outbound channel) is present; a new Level 0 control, CTRL-0097, requires breaking that combination; and a new risk, RISK-055, covers data exfiltration by agents that handle messages, such as email assistants
> - **One rule for Level 0**: a Level 0 control applies wherever its risk is applicable, whatever the risk's impact and likelihood score, and is waived only when the capability or component it concerns is not present; each Level 0 control now matches its subject, so CVE scanning applies only where code runs, tool authentication covers every remote tool, and the memory-write controls concern persistent memory
> - **Human approval as a floor**: human approval of business transactions outside pre-authorised limits, of sensitive official communications, and of deletions that cannot be undone is now Level 0, together with least privilege and checking that approvals remain real decisions; copyright guardrails and code linters move to Level 1
> - **Risks apply where they arise**: multi-agent risks now apply only to systems in which more than one agent works on a task, including agents operated by other organisations, and the sandbox-escape risk only to systems that can execute code, so simpler systems no longer carry Level 0 controls that cannot apply to them
> - **New risks, hazards and crosswalks**: eight risks and eight controls from the 2026 evidence base, including the first risk that arises from a combination of elements; the hazards each risk results in; and crosswalks to the [OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications](https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/), OWASP's agentic threat taxonomy, the [CSA Securing Agentic AI Addendum](https://www.csa.gov.sg/resources/publications/addendum-on-securing-ai-systems/), and [IMDA's Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI](https://www.imda.gov.sg/-/media/imda/files/about/emerging-tech-and-research/artificial-intelligence/mgf-for-agentic-ai.pdf)
> - **A corrected, versioned register**: the links between controls and risks were checked and corrected, and the register now carries a version that can be cited and pinned; every change is in the [Changelog](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/changelog/)
> - **Readable by AI agents**: a [full-text register](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/) with a link for every risk and control, and an [`llms.txt`](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/llms.txt) index for agents
> - **ARC assessment skill**: an [Agent Skill](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft/tree/main/skills) that lets a coding agent assess the system it is building against the register
>
> Earlier (December 2025): the [introduction](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/introduction/) with design rationale and literature review, the unified [Elements](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/elements/) page, the [interactive register](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/risk-register/), the [ARCvisor](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/resources/#arcvisor) tool, and the two technical papers in [Resources](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/resources/).

## About the Authors

The ARC Framework is developed by the Responsible AI team in GovTech Singapore's AI Practice. We develop deep technical capabilities in Responsible AI to improve how the Singapore government develops, evaluates, deploys, and monitors AI systems in a safe, trustworthy, and ethical manner.

In developing this framework, we work closely with other teams in the Singapore government, such as the Ministry for Digital Development and Information, the Cybersecurity Agency of Singapore, and the Infocomm Media Development Authority. We are grateful for their feedback and contributions, which have helped to make this framework more effective, robust, and thorough.

Beyond the [technical governance framework](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/introduction/) and [implementation guide](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/implementation/), we have also developed additional tools and resources to help organisations understand and get started with using the ARC framework to govern their agentic AI systems. 

| Resource | Target Audience | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ARCvisor](#arcvisor) | AI governance teams, developers | Check, review and sign an assessment, with the evidence the ARC skill found in the code |
| [Technical Paper](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/assets/ARC_Framework-Paper-IASEAI_2026.pdf) | AI governance teams, academia | In-depth technical details and research foundations |
| [Baseline Risk Register](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/risk-register/) | AI governance teams, developers | Interactive exploration of 66 risks and 103 controls ([full text](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/); [machine-readable YAML](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft/tree/main/arc-risk-register)) |
| [ARC Assessment Skill](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft/tree/main/skills) | Developers using coding agents | An Agent Skill that lets a coding agent assess the system it is building: capabilities from the code, applicable risks and controls from the register, implementation gaps, and a drafted assessment |
| [Assessment Template](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/implementation/assessment-template/) | AI developers, governance teams | Record of a per-system assessment: capabilities, applicable risks, controls with evidence, residual risks, sign-off |
| [Changelog](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/changelog/) | Everyone using the register | What changed in each register version, and the versioning policy |
| Presentation slides (pending) | General AI-literate audience | High-level overview of the ARC framework |

## ARCvisor

ARCvisor is where people check, decide and sign an ARC assessment. The [ARC skill](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft/tree/main/skills) reads a system's code in the developer's coding agent and writes `docs/arc/assessment.arc.json`. ARCvisor opens that file and keeps the record:

- the system's capabilities and the context each is used in
- the risks that apply, with their scores
- each control's status and evidence
- the residual risks, and who accepted them
- the reviewer's comments and the sign-off

[Open ARCvisor](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arcvisor) [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft/tree/main/web)

- **The register's own rules.** ARCvisor and the skill share one implementation of what applies to a system (`packages/arc-core`). A test checks that it gives the skill's answer for 400 systems.
- **AI suggestions stay suggestions.** Whatever the skill or an AI suggests is accepted, edited or dismissed one item at a time. Nothing it wrote counts until a person decides.
- **Evidence from the code.** Each control shows what the code check found, with the lines it rests on. A Level 0 entry that the code contradicts blocks sign-off until it is fixed or the reviewer accepts the explanation.
- **Review in the same place.** It has comment threads and the reviewer's verdict. It also shows what changed since the last signed revision, and what a new register version adds.
- **Nothing leaves the browser.** Assessments are saved in the browser and in files you keep. There is no server.

The first version of ARCvisor was a conversational assistant, described in the [ARCvisor preprint](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/assets/ARCvisor-Preprint_2025.pdf). Its code stays in `app/` until the new app replaces it.

## Contributing to the register 🤝

The register is a living document and we welcome proposals for new risks, new controls, corrections, and crosswalks. The bar is the same one we hold ourselves to: a risk must be supported by academic research or a documented industry incident, and a control must be actionable, composable, and measurable. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for the entry format, the validator, and the pull-request flow, or [open an issue](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft/issues) if you would rather describe the proposal and let us draft it.

# Capability combinations

<!-- The tables marked "arc:" below are filled in from arc-risk-register/*.yaml when the site is built (scripts/build_risk_register.py). Edit the YAML, not the tables. -->

> **Page Summary**
>
> Some risks belong to no single capability. They arise only when a system holds several capabilities at once. This page explains the four ways capabilities combine, and how ARC handles them: combination rules that bring a risk into scope whenever a system's capabilities can complete the combination, a list of the capabilities that give a system others, and a control for each rule. The lethal trifecta is the worked example.

## Why combinations matter

ARC assesses a system one element at a time. Each [capability](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/elements/) brings its own risks, and each risk has its own controls. That works when the risks are independent of each other.

Some are not. Consider three agents:

- An agent that only browses the web can be misled by what it reads, but it holds nothing worth stealing.
- An agent that only reads internal files holds sensitive data, but no outsider can give it instructions.
- An agent that does both can be told by a web page to open a file and send its contents to an address the attacker chose.

The third agent has a risk that neither of the first two has. Each of its capabilities can be well controlled on its own terms, so an assessment that looks at one capability at a time can pass a system that is exposed.

Other fields met this problem long before agents did. Auditors use [segregation-of-duties matrices](https://www.isaca.org/resources/isaca-journal/issues/2016/volume-3/implementing-segregation-of-duties-a-practical-experience-based-on-best-practices) to find duties that no one person should hold together. Security researchers wrote [rules for dangerous combinations of app permissions](https://doi.org/10.1145/1653662.1653691) on mobile phones. Cloud security tools flag ["toxic combinations"](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/toxic-combinations-overview) of findings that are minor alone. ARC applies the same idea to the capabilities of an agentic system.

## Four ways capabilities combine

| Mechanism | What combines | Example with no attacker | In register 2.0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Flow** | A capability that reads, and one that writes somewhere with a different level of trust | Internal data pasted into a web search; web content saved into official records | The lethal trifecta rule |
| **Reach beyond the declared list** | Code Execution, Computer Use, System Management or Agent Delegation, with anything else | An agent with code execution and network access can call any API, whether or not that capability was declared | [Capabilities that give a system others](#capabilities-that-give-a-system-others) |
| **Both sides of a check** | The capability to do something, and the capability to change what checks it | An agent that writes code and also deploys it, or that acts and can also edit its own logs | The [oversight within reach](#oversight-within-reach) rule, for an agent's own oversight |
| **Loops** | A capability that writes where another reads | Instructions planted in memory or in a file are read back in a later session | Covered for persistent memory by the [Memory component](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/elements/#components); not yet a rule |

The first mechanism has been studied most. The lethal trifecta, Meta's [Agents Rule of Two](https://ai.meta.com/blog/practical-ai-agent-security/) and information-flow defences such as [CaMeL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18813) all address it. The second matters most to a framework like ARC, which assumes that the list of capabilities bounds what a system can do. Four capabilities break that assumption, because they produce or borrow other capabilities.

## What ARC builds in

**Roles.** The register records what each capability can contribute to a combination, for example *untrusted content* or *an outbound channel*. A capability supplies a role wherever it is present (**Yes**), or only in some deployments (**Maybe**, with a note saying when). Some capabilities supply a role only from a certain [authority](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/elements/#context-how-a-capability-is-used) upwards: Official Communication is an outbound channel when the agent sends messages itself, and not when a person sends what it drafts.

**Rules.** A rule names the roles that must all be supplied. Any capability that supplies a role will do, so a rule covers every pairing without listing them. A rule is:

- **present** when every role is supplied by a capability marked Yes;
- **possible** when every role is supplied, at least one only by capabilities marked Maybe;
- **not present** when at least one role is supplied by none of the system's capabilities.

A rule that is present or possible brings its risks into scope, and its control must be implemented unless the assessor shows that a role is absent. The roles, rules and marks are in [`combinations.yaml`](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft/blob/main/arc-risk-register/combinations.yaml), next to the risks and controls.

**Composite risks.** A risk can also list more than one element, and then applies only when the system has all of them. These risks arise from a rule or from several elements:

| Risk | Applies when |
| --- | --- |
| [RISK-012](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/#RISK-012) Cascading errors in multi-agent architectures | The system has all of: Agentic Architecture (DSN-01) + Agent Delegation (CAP-02) |
| [RISK-013](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/#RISK-013) Man-in-the-middle attacks between agents | The system has all of: Agentic Architecture (DSN-01) + Agent Delegation (CAP-02) |
| [RISK-047](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/#RISK-047) Data exfiltration through combined access to untrusted content, sensitive data, and an outbound channel | The rule "Lethal trifecta" is present or possible: the system's capabilities can supply untrusted content, sensitive data, outbound channel |
| [RISK-049](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/#RISK-049) Escape from evaluation or sandbox containment onto live systems | The system has all of: Roles and Access Controls (DSN-02) + Code Execution (CAP-10) |
| [RISK-051](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/#RISK-051) Unsanctioned coordination between agents | The system has all of: Agentic Architecture (DSN-01) + Agent Delegation (CAP-02) |
| [RISK-053](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/#RISK-053) Dependence on third-party agents as counterparties or delegates | The system has all of: Protocols (CMP-05) + Agent Delegation (CAP-02) |
| [RISK-062](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/#RISK-062) Agent alters or disables the oversight placed on it | The rule "Oversight within reach" is present or possible: the system's capabilities can supply its own safeguards |

Register 2.0 has two rules: the lethal trifecta, and oversight within reach.

## The lethal trifecta

An agent holds the lethal trifecta, a term coined by [Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Jun/16/the-lethal-trifecta/), when it has all three of the following:

1. **Untrusted content.** Content that someone outside the organisation's control can write reaches the agent.
2. **Sensitive data.** The agent can read data that would cause harm if it left the organisation.
3. **An outbound channel.** The agent can cause data to reach a destination outside the organisation's control.

LLMs cannot reliably tell instructions from data, so text in a web page, an email, or a document can direct an agent that reads it. With all three legs in place, one injected instruction is enough. The agent reads the sensitive data and sends it out through a channel it is allowed to use. No control is bypassed, because every step is something the agent is permitted to do.

This has happened. In [EchoLeak](https://www.hackthebox.com/blog/cve-2025-32711-echoleak-copilot-vulnerability), a single crafted email led Microsoft 365 Copilot to send internal data to an attacker. In [ForcedLeak](https://www.varonis.com/blog/forcedleak), instructions in a web-form submission led Salesforce Agentforce to send out customer records. The Frontier Model Forum's [brief on agent security](https://www.frontiermodelforum.org/uploads/2026/06/FMF-Issue-Brief-on-Emerging-Security-Practices-for-AI-Agents.pdf) recommends that, in higher-risk uses, no agent hold all three. Meta's [Agents Rule of Two](https://ai.meta.com/blog/practical-ai-agent-security/) gives similar advice.

### Which capabilities supply each leg

A capability can supply a leg wherever it is present, or only in some deployments.

| Capability | Untrusted content | Sensitive data | Outbound channel |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Planning and Goal Management (CAP-01) | – | – | – |
| Agent Delegation (CAP-02) | Maybe | – | Maybe |
| Tool Use (CAP-03) | – | – | – |
| Multimodal Understanding and Generation (CAP-04) | Maybe | – | Maybe |
| Official Communication (CAP-05) | Maybe | – | **Yes** |
| Business Transactions (CAP-06) | – | Maybe | **Yes** |
| Internet and Search Access (CAP-07) | **Yes** | – | **Yes** |
| Computer Use (CAP-08) | **Yes** | **Yes** | **Yes** |
| Other Programmatic Interfaces (CAP-09) | Maybe | Maybe | Maybe |
| Code Execution (CAP-10) | Maybe | – | Maybe |
| File and Data Management (CAP-11) | Maybe | **Yes** | – |
| System Management (CAP-12) | – | **Yes** | Maybe |

**Yes** means the capability supplies the leg wherever it is present. **Maybe** means it depends on the deployment, and the notes below say when. Planning and Goal Management and Tool Use supply no leg by themselves.

> **When each capability supplies a leg**
>
> **Untrusted content.** Content that someone outside the organisation's control can write reaches the agent.
>
> - Agent Delegation (CAP-02): maybe. Yes if it takes output from agents that other parties operate, or from agents that read untrusted content themselves.
> - Multimodal Understanding and Generation (CAP-04): maybe. Yes if its users are members of the public, or can upload or paste documents, images, or audio that someone else wrote.
> - Official Communication (CAP-05): maybe. Yes if it also reads replies or other inbound messages on the channels it sends through.
> - Internet and Search Access (CAP-07): yes. Web pages and search results can be written by anyone.
> - Computer Use (CAP-08): yes. Whatever appears on screen reaches the agent, including web pages, emails, and documents written by others.
> - Other Programmatic Interfaces (CAP-09): maybe. Yes if any API, queue, or mailbox it reads carries content from outside parties, such as inbound email, support tickets, form submissions, or webhooks.
> - Code Execution (CAP-10): maybe. Yes if it runs or reads code, packages, or repositories that outside parties can change.
> - File and Data Management (CAP-11): maybe. Yes if any file or data store it reads holds content from outside parties, such as uploads, shared drives, or records created from customer input.
>
> **Sensitive data.** The agent can read data that would cause harm if it left the organisation, such as personal data, credentials, or confidential records.
>
> - Business Transactions (CAP-06): maybe. Yes if it holds payment credentials, or can read account, order, or customer records.
> - Computer Use (CAP-08): yes. It can see whatever the signed-in user can open on the machine.
> - Other Programmatic Interfaces (CAP-09): maybe. Yes if any API it can call returns personal, confidential, or credential data.
> - File and Data Management (CAP-11): yes. It reads the organisation's files, databases, or knowledge bases.
> - System Management (CAP-12): yes. System administration reaches configuration, credentials, and logs.
>
> **Outbound channel.** The agent can cause data to reach a destination outside the organisation's control.
>
> - Agent Delegation (CAP-02): maybe. Yes if it can pass data to an agent that another party operates, or to an agent that has an outbound channel of its own.
> - Multimodal Understanding and Generation (CAP-04): maybe. Yes if its output is shown to people outside the organisation, or is rendered in a way that loads external images or links.
> - Official Communication (CAP-05): yes, from act with approval upwards. It sends messages to people outside the organisation.
> - Business Transactions (CAP-06): yes, from act with approval upwards. Transactions carry data to external parties in payment references, order details, and booking fields.
> - Internet and Search Access (CAP-07): yes. Any request to a web address can carry data in the URL or the query.
> - Computer Use (CAP-08): yes. It can use any application on the machine that sends data, including the browser and the mail client.
> - Other Programmatic Interfaces (CAP-09): maybe. Yes if any API it can call writes to a system outside the organisation, or accepts a destination that the agent chooses.
> - Code Execution (CAP-10): maybe, from act with approval upwards. Yes if the environment its code runs in can make network requests.
> - System Management (CAP-12): maybe, from act with approval upwards. Yes if it can change network, sharing, or access settings so that data becomes reachable from outside.

Components are not in the table. Persistent [memory](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/elements/) can carry untrusted content or sensitive data from one session into a later one, so count what memory holds when you answer for each leg.

### The verdict

| Verdict | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Present** | Every leg is supplied by a capability marked Yes | Implement the control below |
| **Possible** | Every leg is supplied, but at least one only by capabilities marked Maybe | Answer the note for each of those capabilities from the system's code and configuration. If every leg is confirmed, implement the control. If a leg is absent, waive the control and record the evidence |
| **Not present** | At least one leg is supplied by no capability | Waive the control wherever it is listed, and record which leg is absent |

The control is:

> **[CTRL-0097](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/#CTRL-0097) (Level 0 · Cardinal).** Do not give one agent untrusted content, access to sensitive data, and an unrestricted outbound channel at once; remove one, or gate the outbound channel outside the agent.

It is a [Level 0 control](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/controls/#control-levels). Scoring does not waive it. It is waived only when a leg is absent, in the same way that any Level 0 control is waived when the capability or component it concerns is not present.

There are three ways to break the combination:

- **Split the agent.** Give the untrusted content to a separate agent that has no access to sensitive data and returns only structured values.
- **Remove the data.** Take away the sensitive data that the task does not need.
- **Gate the channel.** Restrict the outbound channel outside the agent. Limit recipients and destinations to a fixed allowlist, and require human approval for any message or call that carries data to a new recipient.

The verdict describes the system as a whole. The control applies to each agent, so in a multi-agent system, record which agent holds each leg. Splitting the legs across agents satisfies the control only if the agent that reads untrusted content cannot pass free text to the agent that holds the data or the channel.

### Try it

Tick the capabilities your system has. The check runs in your browser, and nothing is sent anywhere.

### Worked examples

These are the systems from the [guide for AI developers](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/implementation/for-ai-developers/#application-examples), with a simple question-answering bot for comparison.

The verdicts below assume the most cautious context for each capability.

| System | Capabilities | Verdict | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Question-answering bot | CAP-04 | **Not present** | Nothing supplies sensitive data |
| Agentic fact checker | CAP-01, 02, 03, 04, 07, 11 | **Present** | Internet and Search Access supplies untrusted content and an outbound channel; File and Data Management supplies sensitive data |
| Agentic coding assistant | CAP-01, 02, 03, 04, 10, 11 | **Possible** | File and Data Management supplies sensitive data. Untrusted content depends on whether it reads repositories or packages that others can change. An outbound channel depends on whether its code runs with network access |
| Agentic call assistant | CAP-01, 02, 04, 06, 09, 11 | **Possible** | File and Data Management supplies sensitive data, and Business Transactions supplies an outbound channel. Untrusted content depends on what its callers and the systems it reads can put in front of it |

## Oversight within reach

The second rule is the simplest case of holding both sides of a check: an agent that can change the logs, monitors, permissions, approval settings, or configuration that are meant to constrain it. Agents have done this in pursuit of a task, with no attacker involved, and have been made to do it by injected content. The rule has one role.

| Capability | Its own safeguards |
| --- | :---: |
| Planning and Goal Management (CAP-01) | – |
| Agent Delegation (CAP-02) | – |
| Tool Use (CAP-03) | – |
| Multimodal Understanding and Generation (CAP-04) | – |
| Official Communication (CAP-05) | – |
| Business Transactions (CAP-06) | – |
| Internet and Search Access (CAP-07) | – |
| Computer Use (CAP-08) | Maybe |
| Other Programmatic Interfaces (CAP-09) | – |
| Code Execution (CAP-10) | Maybe |
| File and Data Management (CAP-11) | Maybe |
| System Management (CAP-12) | **Yes** |

> **When each capability supplies the role**
>
> **Its own safeguards.** The agent can change the logs, monitors, permissions, approval settings, or configuration that are meant to constrain it.
>
> - Computer Use (CAP-08): maybe. Yes if it can open the settings of the application or platform that runs it.
> - Code Execution (CAP-10): maybe, from act with approval upwards. Yes if code it runs can reach the files, services, or settings that hold its permissions, approvals, logs, or monitors.
> - File and Data Management (CAP-11): maybe, from act with approval upwards. Yes if its write access covers its own instruction, configuration, or log files.
> - System Management (CAP-12): yes, from act with approval upwards. It manages access controls, monitoring, and configuration, which can include its own.

When the rule is present or possible, [RISK-062](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/#RISK-062) is in scope and this control applies:

> **[CTRL-0101](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/#CTRL-0101) (Level 0 · Cardinal).** Give agents no write access to their own instructions, configuration, permissions, logs, or monitors.

A capability used only to read does not supply the role. The control is met when no identity, tool, or code path the agent has can write to what governs it, which is something to check for code execution and computer use as well as for the agent's named tools.

## Capabilities that give a system others

ARC assesses a system by the capabilities it declares. Four capabilities can give a system more than was declared: code can call anything its environment lets it reach, a computer-use agent can open any application, an administrator can grant itself access, and a delegating agent borrows what its delegates can do. Controls placed on the agent's named tools do not bind what it does by these routes.

| Capability | Also gives the system | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent Delegation (CAP-02) | Any capability | Maybe. The system has every capability held by an agent it can delegate to, including agents that another party operates. List those agents and their capabilities. |
| Computer Use (CAP-08) | Internet and Search Access (CAP-07) | Maybe. Yes if a browser is installed on the machine it operates. |
| Computer Use (CAP-08) | Other Programmatic Interfaces (CAP-09) | Maybe. Yes if the machine has applications or a terminal that call other systems. |
| Computer Use (CAP-08) | Code Execution (CAP-10) | Maybe. Yes if it can open a terminal, a code editor, or any application that runs scripts. |
| Computer Use (CAP-08) | File and Data Management (CAP-11) | Yes. It can open, change, and delete whatever files the signed-in user can. |
| Computer Use (CAP-08) | System Management (CAP-12) | Maybe. Yes if the signed-in user can change system settings or access controls. |
| Code Execution (CAP-10) | Other Programmatic Interfaces (CAP-09) | Maybe. Yes unless the environment its code runs in blocks network access. |
| Code Execution (CAP-10) | File and Data Management (CAP-11) | Yes. Code can read and write whatever files the account it runs under can. |
| Code Execution (CAP-10) | System Management (CAP-12) | Maybe. Yes if credentials for infrastructure, deployment, or administration are within reach of the code it runs. |
| System Management (CAP-12) | File and Data Management (CAP-11) | Maybe. Yes if it can grant itself access to data stores it was not given. |

For each row that applies to a system, either add the implied capability to the assessment, or record the evidence that it does not apply, such as a sandbox with no network access and no credentials in reach.

## Using the check in an assessment

- **In the developer guide:** the check is part of [Step 2](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/implementation/for-ai-developers/#step-2-evaluate-risks), after the applicable risks are listed.
- **In the assessment template:** [Section 2a](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/implementation/assessment-template/#2a-capability-combinations) records the verdict, the answer for each leg, and how the combination is broken.
- **With a coding agent:** the [ARC assessment skill](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft/tree/main/skills) runs the check. `arc.py assess` prints the verdict and the notes to answer for the capabilities given.

## Limits

- **Two rules so far.** Register 2.0 has rules for the lethal trifecta and for an agent's reach over its own oversight. Other pairings of a capability with the check on it, such as writing code and deploying it, and loops other than persistent memory, are described above but have no rule yet.
- **Capabilities are coarse.** Internet and Search Access covers reading pages and posting to them. Many systems will therefore get a verdict of Possible, and the notes turn that verdict into questions that evidence can answer.
- **Implied capabilities are reported, not added.** The check lists the capabilities a system probably also has. It leaves the decision to the assessor, who adds them or records why they do not apply.
- **Design time only.** The check reads what a system can do, not what it does in a given session. [CTRL-0090](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/register-full-text/#CTRL-0090) covers enforcement at run time.

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/keeping-current/

# Keeping the register current

> **Page Summary**
>
> Agentic systems change faster than a register can be rewritten. This page explains how ARC is kept in step with what actually goes wrong: an incident file that every proposed change is checked against, a quarterly review, reference systems that guard the tools against regressions, and the validation that has not been done yet.

## The incident file

ARC keeps a [curated file of incidents](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft/tree/main/incidents), vulnerabilities and research findings that involve agentic systems. Each case is mapped to the elements where the failure arose and to the risks in the register that describe it. A case that no risk describes is filed under a gap theme.

The file is not an incident database. It draws on those that exist, and adds two things: a selection made from the point of view of someone building or deploying an agent, and the mapping to this register. It answers two questions.

- **Which cases does the register not describe?** These are candidates for new risks and controls. The twelve risks added in version 2.0 came from this question.
- **Which risks have no case behind them?** These rest on argument or research alone. That can be justified, but it should be a decision.

## The quarterly review

Four steps, described in full in the incident file's own guide:

1. **Harvest.** A script lists new leads from the upstream trackers that publish machine-readable data, and drops anything already seen.
2. **Triage.** Each lead becomes a case or is logged as left out, with a reason. An agent can prepare this from written rules; a maintainer reviews it.
3. **Verify.** A maintainer opens the primary source for every case of harm and every case with a gap.
4. **Review.** The coverage report is read against the previous one.

A change to the register is proposed when:

- a gap theme has **three or more cases, at least one of them harm, from more than one source**. It becomes a proposal for a new risk or control, with the cases as its evidence;
- a risk has **no case** after two reviews. It is checked: is it still credible, and is it worded so that a case could match it?
- a control's **level** no longer matches the evidence, in either direction.

Proposals go through the register's normal change process and appear in the [changelog](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/changelog/).

## What the file cannot tell you

- **How often things happen.** The file holds what was published, in English, and found by the trackers it draws on. Security research and coding agents are over-represented. Quiet operational failures inside organisations are under-represented.
- **Whether a control works.** A case shows that something went wrong. It rarely shows which control would have stopped it.

## Reference systems

The repository holds [profiles of four example systems](https://github.com/govtech-responsibleai/arc-v2-draft/tree/main/examples/systems): a question-answering bot and the three worked examples in the [guide for AI developers](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/implementation/for-ai-developers/). A profile lists a system's capabilities, how each is used, and its conditional components.

They do two jobs. The numbers quoted in the developer guide are checked against the assessment tool on every change, so the guide cannot drift from the register. And any tool that implements ARC can be run on the same profiles and compared.

## Validation still to do

Neither ARCvisor nor the assessment skill has been validated against expert assessments. The plan:

1. Add reference systems until they cover every capability and both conditional components.
2. Have two people who know ARC assess each one independently, and record where they differ. The differences show where the register is ambiguous.
3. Run each tool on the same systems and compare three things with the agreed assessments: the capabilities identified, the risks marked as priorities, and whether every Level 0 control is addressed.
4. Publish the agreement rates with each release.

Until this is done, treat a tool's output as a draft for a person to review.

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-01/

# CAP-01 · Planning and Goal Management

ARC element (capability, Cognitive), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-01/

The capability to develop detailed, step-by-step, and executable plans with specific tasks in response to broad instructions. This includes prioritizing activities based on importance and dependencies between tasks, monitoring how well its plan is working, and adjusting when circumstances change or obstacles arise.

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-019: Generating plans that fail to meet the user's requirements
- RISK-020: Generating plans that overlook safety implications
- RISK-057: Pursuit of a goal by means the principal did not sanction

---

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-02/

# CAP-02 · Agent Delegation

ARC element (capability, Cognitive), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-02/

The capability to assign subtasks to other agents and coordinate their activities to achieve broader goals. This includes identifying which components are best suited for specific tasks, issuing clear instructions, managing inter-agent dependencies, and monitoring performance or failures. A system has this capability whenever more than one agent works on a task, whether an agent decides the hand-offs or they are fixed in the workflow, and whether the other agents belong to the same system or are operated by another party, including agents it transacts with as counterparties.

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-012: Cascading errors in multi-agent architectures
- RISK-013: Man-in-the-middle attacks between agents
- RISK-021: Incorrect task delegation between agents
- RISK-022: Malicious or manipulative use of delegated agents
- RISK-051: Unsanctioned coordination between agents
- RISK-053: Dependence on third-party agents as counterparties or delegates
- RISK-063: Authority passing between agents without a check

---

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-03/

# CAP-03 · Tool Use

ARC element (capability, Cognitive), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-03/

The capability to evaluate available options and choose the best tool for specific subtasks, based on the capabilities and limitations of different tools and matching them appropriately to the tasks. This includes selecting between search, computation, code execution, or domain-specific APIs, determining when tool invocation is necessary, and sequencing or combining multiple tools to complete complex tasks effectively.

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-023: Incorrect tool selection or misuse

---

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-04/

# CAP-04 · Multimodal Understanding and Generation

ARC element (capability, Interaction), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-04/

The capability to communicate with human users across multiple modalities, including natural language conversation (explaining topics, generating documents, interactive discussions) and multimodal understanding/generation (processing and creating image, audio, or video content such as visual analysis, speech transcription, or multimedia creation).

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-024: Generation of undesirable content
- RISK-025: Generation of unqualified advice in specialised domains
- RISK-026: Generation of controversial or sensitive content
- RISK-027: Regurgitating personally identifiable information
- RISK-028: Generation of non-factual or hallucinated content
- RISK-029: Generation of copyrighted content

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-05/

# CAP-05 · Official Communication

ARC element (capability, Interaction), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-05/

The capability to compose, finalise, and dispatch authoritative communications that formally and legally represent an organization to external parties (e.g. customers, partners, regulators, courts, or media) via approved channels and formats, thereby creating potential legal, regulatory, or reputational obligations. This includes sending legally binding correspondence, publishing official statements or press releases, and responding to external inquiries using the organisation's identity. A system has this capability whether a person sends what the agent drafts, approves each message before it goes, or lets the agent send by itself; that difference is recorded as the capability's authority.

Used at: propose, act with approval, act alone; irreversible: always; external: always

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-030: Misrepresentation of authorship
- RISK-031: Inaccurate promises or statements in official communications

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-06/

# CAP-06 · Business Transactions

ARC element (capability, Interaction), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-06/

The capability to initiate, authorise, and execute binding business transactions with external parties - such as payments, purchases, reservations, or service commitments - resulting in real financial, contractual, or operational obligations for the organization. This includes processing payments or refunds, placing orders or subscriptions, booking services or reservations, and accepting or triggering contractual commitments on behalf of the organization. A system has this capability whether a person completes the transactions the agent prepares, approves each one, or lets the agent transact by itself within limits set in advance; that difference is recorded as the capability's authority.

Used at: propose, act with approval, act alone; irreversible: ask; external: always

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-032: Unauthorised execution of business transactions
- RISK-033: Leakage of transaction credentials

# CAP-07 · Internet and Search Access

ARC element (capability, Interaction), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-07/

The capability to autonomously access, browse, search, and retrieve information from the Internet to augment the LLM's static training knowledge with external and up-to-date sources in support of task execution and response generation. This includes issuing search queries, following and parsing web pages, extracting relevant facts or documents, and aggregating information from multiple online sources.

Used at: read; irreversible: never; external: always

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-034: Prompt injection via malicious websites
- RISK-035: Unreliable information or websites

# CAP-08 · Computer Use

ARC element (capability, Interaction), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-08/

The capability to directly operate a computer’s graphical user interface on behalf of the user, enabling the agent to navigate applications and execute tasks through mouse, keyboard, and window-based interactions. This includes moving the cursor, clicking buttons, entering text, using keyboard shortcuts, switching between windows and applications, and navigating files and menus within the operating system environment.

Used at: act with approval, act alone; irreversible: ask; external: ask

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-036: Prompt injection risks through computer use
- RISK-037: Exposure of sensitive data

# CAP-09 · Other Programmatic Interfaces

ARC element (capability, Interaction), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-09/

The capability to interact with external systems through non-graphical, programmatic interfaces, such as APIs, SDKs, and backend services, to exchange data or trigger actions as part of task execution. This includes calling REST or GraphQL APIs, invoking cloud services, publishing or consuming messages from queues or event streams, and performing operations such as code pushes, data updates, or system integrations across enterprise platforms. This includes sending and receiving email, chat, or other messages through an API or mail protocol, including when those messages are also Official Communication (CAP-05).

Used at: read, propose, act with approval, act alone; irreversible: ask; external: ask

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-038: Incorrect use of unfamiliar programmatic interfaces
- RISK-059: Prompt injection through inbound messages

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-10/

# CAP-10 · Code Execution

ARC element (capability, Operational), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-10/

The capability to write, execute, and debug code in various programming languages to automate tasks or solve computational problems. This includes implementing algorithms, writing scripts, compiling and running code, debugging errors, and integrating with external systems through APIs or backend services.

Used at: propose, act with approval, act alone; irreversible: ask; external: ask

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-039: Production or execution of poor or ineffective code
- RISK-040: Production or execution of vulnerable or malicious code
- RISK-049: Escape from evaluation or sandbox containment onto live systems
- RISK-056: Actions beyond the agent's tools through code execution and reachable credentials

# CAP-11 · File and Data Management

ARC element (capability, Operational), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-11/

The capability to manage the full lifecycle of files and data by creating, reading, modifying, organizing, converting, querying, and updating information across both unstructured artifacts (e.g. documents, spreadsheets, media files) and structured data stores (e.g. SQL/NoSQL databases, data warehouses, vector or embedding stores) in support of operational tasks. This includes ingesting and transforming datasets, generating or updating files, maintaining directory or schema structures, executing database queries or updates, and storing or retrieving embeddings or derived data products.

Used at: read, propose, act with approval, act alone; irreversible: ask; external: ask

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-041: Unintended overwriting or deletion of files or data
- RISK-042: Database overload due to inefficient data operations
- RISK-043: Exposure of sensitive data through file or database access
- RISK-044: Prompt injection via malicious files or data
- RISK-066: Personal data collected, kept, or passed on beyond what the task needs

# CAP-12 · System Management

ARC element (capability, Operational), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cap-12/

The capability to directly manage and configure technical systems and infrastructure by adjusting system settings, controlling computing resources, and administering operational environments across on-premise or cloud platforms. This includes monitoring system health and performance, managing authentication credentials and access controls, provisioning or scaling compute and storage resources, configuring operating system or runtime parameters, and applying system-level optimisations to support reliable operation.

Used at: read, propose, act with approval, act alone; irreversible: ask; external: ask

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-045: Misconfiguration of system resources
- RISK-046: System overload due to inefficient or excessive operations

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cmp-01/

# CMP-01 · LLM

ARC element (component), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cmp-01/

A large language model (LLM) is a neural network trained on massive text data to learn statistical patterns of language, enabling it to understand, generate, and reason over natural language inputs. It is the core reasoning engine that processes instructions, interprets user inputs, and generates contextually appropriate responses by leveraging its trained language understanding and generation capabilities. There are a large variety of LLMs to choose from, with different sizes, capabilities, and architectures, from large closed-source model families such as OpenAI's GPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Google's Gemini, to open-weights families such as Llama, Qwen, and Mistral, which include small models that can run on local hardware.

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-001: Use of untrusted or compromised LLMs
- RISK-002: Insufficient alignment of LLM behaviour
- RISK-003: Insufficient LLM capability and reliability
- RISK-050: Deceptive behaviour toward overseers
- RISK-061: Dependence on a model provider

---

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cmp-02/

# CMP-02 · Instructions

ARC element (component), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cmp-02/

Instructions are structured inputs provided to an LLM that define the task, constraints, and context, guiding how the model interprets inputs and generates outputs. They guide the LLM's decision process by conditioning prompts and tool use with objectives, policies, and guardrails. Forms include system prompts, policies, schemas, and rubrics, varying by framework and enforcement strictness.

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-008: Vague or underspecified instructions
- RISK-009: Unsanitised inputs in system instructions
- RISK-058: Instruction and configuration files as a way in
- RISK-067: Use of the agent by its own principal against others

---

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cmp-03/

# CMP-03 · Tools

ARC element (component), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cmp-03/

Tools are external functions, APIs, or resources attached to an LLM that extend its capabilities beyond text generation, enabling it to retrieve information, execute actions, and affect external systems (e.g., search, code execution, database queries, or file manipulation), typically through structured interfaces such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that constrain invocation, inputs, permissions, and outputs for agentic control and safety.

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-004: Weak tool authentication and authorisation controls
- RISK-005: Lack of proper role-based access control for tools
- RISK-007: Lack of input sanitisation
- RISK-048: Compromise through the tool, skill, and dependency supply chain

---

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cmp-04/

# CMP-04 · Memory

ARC element (component), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cmp-04/

Memory is a persistent or semi-persistent data store attached to an LLM that retains information across interactions—such as conversation history, user preferences, task state, and retrieved knowledge—enabling continuity, long-horizon reasoning, and personalization in agentic workflows. Memory may be implemented through mechanisms such as context windows, vector databases, episodic logs, or external state stores, each offering different trade-offs in latency, fidelity, and persistence. Every agent has working memory, the context it carries within a task; a system has persistent memory when it keeps information beyond a single session or shares it across users or tasks.

Conditional: present when The system keeps information beyond a single session, or shares it across users or tasks.

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-010: Poisoned memory
- RISK-011: Sensitive data leakage across memory contexts

---

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cmp-05/

# CMP-05 · Protocols

ARC element (component), register 2.0.0-draft.1. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/cmp-05/

Protocols are the standard interfaces through which an agentic system connects to tools, services, and agents that another party builds or operates, such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for tool servers and agent-to-agent protocols such as A2A. A protocol governs how the other party is discovered, how it is identified and authenticated, what it declares about itself to the agent (tool descriptions, capability lists, agent cards), and how requests and results pass between the two. A system has this component when it makes at least one such connection, in either direction: its agents reach another party's tool server or agent, or another party's agents reach it. A function or API wrapper that the system's own team writes is a tool, not a protocol connection, because the team controls the description the agent sees.

Conditional: present when At least one tool server or agent that another party builds or operates is connected to the system through an agent protocol such as MCP or A2A, in either direction.

## Risks that arise from it

- RISK-006: Tool poisoning by malicious actors
- RISK-053: Dependence on third-party agents as counterparties or delegates
- RISK-064: Harm from a connected tool server or agent to the system that connects to it

---

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/controls/

# All controls

Each control addresses one or more risks. Level 0 controls are adopted as is wherever their risk applies, and some controls are stricter where a capability is used with more authority; see [control levels](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/arc_framework/controls/#control-levels).

## Level 0: adopt as is

46 controls.

## Retired

- [CTRL-0006](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0006/) · Require human approval before executing high-impact actions: replaced by [CTRL-0042](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0042/)
- [CTRL-0014](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0014/) · Use only MCP servers from verified and trusted developers: replaced by [CTRL-0091](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0091/)

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/crosswalks/csa/

# Crosswalk: CSA Securing Agentic AI addendum

ARC maps its controls to [CSA Singapore – Securing Agentic AI, an Addendum to the Guidelines and Companion Guide on Securing AI Systems](https://www.csa.gov.sg/resources/publications/addendum-on-securing-ai-systems/) (1.0 (17 June 2026)). Each mapping points to the nearest corresponding entry; it is not a claim that the two are the same.

Read it from either side: below, each item in that framework lists the ARC entries that map to it, and each ARC entry's own page lists its crosswalks.

## 2.1 · Supply chain security – ensure components are from trusted sources

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0001](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0001/) (Level 0): Use only LLMs from verified and trusted model developers
- [CTRL-0002](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0002/) (Level 0): Obtain legally binding no-training and no-logging agreements from LLM API service providers
- [CTRL-0003](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0003/) (Level 1): Use only established and verified model loaders in production environments
- [CTRL-0004](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0004/) (Level 2): Review the LLM's system card to inform risk assessment and model selection
- [CTRL-0009](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0009/) (Level 0): Use only tool servers and APIs, including MCP servers, that implement robust authentication mechanisms in production environments
- [CTRL-0061](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0061/) (Level 1): Use structured retrieval APIs for web searches rather than web scraping
- [CTRL-0063](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0063/) (Level 1): Prioritise search results from verified, high-quality domains
- [CTRL-0083](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0083/) (Level 0): Disallow unknown or external files unless they have been scanned for threats
- [CTRL-0091](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0091/) (Level 0): Require verified provenance for tools, skills, and dependencies, and re-verify them on every update
- [CTRL-0095](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0095/) (Level 1): Apply due diligence and technical bounds to third-party agents before delegating to them or transacting with them
- [CTRL-0100](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0100/) (Level 0): Load instruction, settings, and tool-configuration files only from locations the operator controls, and ask before using any that arrive with a workspace

## 2.2 · Consider model hardening

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0005](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0005/) (Level 1): Conduct structured evaluation of multiple LLMs for instruction-following, performance, and safety before deployment

## 2.3 · Harden the system beyond the model itself

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0016](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0016/) (Level 0): Define clearly the agent's role, scope, and non-goals in the system prompt
- [CTRL-0017](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0017/) (Level 1): Define clear success criteria for the agent's tasks
- [CTRL-0096](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0096/) (Level 0): Harden agent frameworks and runtimes before exposing them, and patch framework vulnerabilities promptly

## 2.4 · Identify, track and protect AI system assets

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0039](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0039/) (Level 1): Ensure each agent publishes standardised, machine-readable capability descriptors accessible to other agents
- [CTRL-0041](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0041/) (Level 0): Provide comprehensive descriptions for each tool including intended use, required inputs, and potential outputs
- [CTRL-0067](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0067/) (Level 0): Ensure proper documentation of programmatic interfaces for agent use
- [CTRL-0091](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0091/) (Level 0): Require verified provenance for tools, skills, and dependencies, and re-verify them on every update
- [CTRL-0102](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0102/) (Level 1): Issue agents short-lived, task-scoped credentials, keep an inventory of them, and revoke them when an agent or integration is retired

## 2.5 · Have regular backups in the event of compromise

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0077](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0077/) (Level 0): Enable versioning or soft-delete for managed object stores to allow recovery from accidental modifications

## 2.6 · Implement authentication, authorisation and access controls

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0010](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0010/) (Level 1): Use only MCP servers that validate credentials on every inbound request
- [CTRL-0011](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0011/) (Level 0): Limit token scopes to the minimum privileges required and avoid broad or wildcard scopes
- [CTRL-0021](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0021/) (Level 0): Implement allowlists and denylists to restrict what categories of information can be written to the agent's persistent memory
- [CTRL-0025](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0025/) (Level 1): Ensure all inter-agent communications are encrypted in transit and prohibit plaintext channels
- [CTRL-0026](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0026/) (Level 1): Require all agents to authenticate with verifiable, cryptographically signed identities before processing requests
- [CTRL-0030](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0030/) (Level 1): Assign each agent a unique, verifiable identity with no shared credentials
- [CTRL-0031](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0031/) (Level 1): Use only MCP servers that validate token provenance and prohibit unauthorised token passthrough
- [CTRL-0089](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0089/) (Level 0): Enforce default-deny network egress for agent runtimes, allowing only approved destinations
- [CTRL-0098](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0098/) (Level 0): Keep credentials and backups out of reach of agent-run code
- [CTRL-0101](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0101/) (Level 0): Give agents no write access to their own instructions, configuration, permissions, logs, or monitors
- [CTRL-0102](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0102/) (Level 1): Issue agents short-lived, task-scoped credentials, keep an inventory of them, and revoke them when an agent or integration is retired
- [CTRL-0104](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0104/) (Level 1): Authorise each action against the principal it is done for, at the agent that carries it out
- [CTRL-0105](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0105/) (Level 1): Accept instructions and approvals only through a channel that proves they come from the principal

## 2.7 · Implement controls to limit what models or agents can access and generate

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0021](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0021/) (Level 0): Implement allowlists and denylists to restrict what categories of information can be written to the agent's persistent memory
- [CTRL-0024](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0024/) (Level 0): Define formal schemas for inter-agent messages and validate all messages against these schemas before processing
- [CTRL-0037](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0037/) (Level 1): Require planning agents to include explicit safety constraints in all generated plans before execution
- [CTRL-0040](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0040/) (Level 0): Limit the scope of agent actions through predefined thresholds and baselines
- [CTRL-0054](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0054/) (Level 1): Limit agent communications to standard processes with predefined templates
- [CTRL-0064](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0064/) (Level 1): Limit computer use to accessing only safe and trusted resources
- [CTRL-0073](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0073/) (Level 0): Create a denylist of commands that agents are not permitted to execute
- [CTRL-0082](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0082/) (Level 2): Do not grant agents access to personally identifiable or sensitive data unless strictly required
- [CTRL-0084](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0084/) (Level 0): Set minimum and maximum limits on what agents can modify within system resources
- [CTRL-0097](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0097/) (Level 0): Do not give one agent untrusted content, access to sensitive data, and an unrestricted outbound channel at once; remove one, or gate the outbound channel outside the agent
- [CTRL-0099](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0099/) (Level 1): Stop the task when an action is refused and report to a human, instead of letting the agent look for another route
- [CTRL-0106](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0106/) (Level 1): Minimise the personal data an agent sends through its tools, and set a retention period for what it keeps
- [CTRL-0107](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0107/) (Level 1): Set limits on what users may direct the agent to do to others, enforce them across a whole task, and have the agent identify itself

## 2.8 · Apply least privilege; secure-by-default configurations

- [CTRL-0098](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0098/) (Level 0): Keep credentials and backups out of reach of agent-run code

# Crosswalk: Five Eyes guidance on agentic AI

ARC maps its controls to [ASD's ACSC, CISA, NSA, Cyber Centre, NCSC-NZ and NCSC-UK – Careful adoption of agentic AI services](https://www.cyber.gov.au/publication/careful-adoption-of-agentic-ai-services) (May 2026 (published 1 May 2026)). Each mapping points to the nearest corresponding entry; it is not a claim that the two are the same.

Read it from either side: below, each item in that framework lists the ARC entries that map to it, and each ARC entry's own page lists its crosswalks.

# Crosswalk: IMDA Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI

ARC maps its controls to [IMDA – Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI](https://www.imda.gov.sg/-/media/imda/files/about/emerging-tech-and-research/artificial-intelligence/mgf-for-agentic-ai.pdf) (1.5 (May 2026)). Each mapping points to the nearest corresponding entry; it is not a claim that the two are the same.

Read it from either side: below, each item in that framework lists the ARC entries that map to it, and each ARC entry's own page lists its crosswalks.

## 2.1.1 · Determine suitable use cases

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0004](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0004/) (Level 2): Review the LLM's system card to inform risk assessment and model selection
