- [CTRL-0069](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0069/) (Level 0): Run agent-generated code only in isolated compute environments with network access blocked by default
- [CTRL-0073](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0073/) (Level 0): Create a denylist of commands that agents are not permitted to execute
- [CTRL-0075](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0075/) (Level 1): Do not grant write access to agents unless strictly necessary
- [CTRL-0077](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0077/) (Level 0): Enable versioning or soft-delete for managed object stores to allow recovery from accidental modifications
- [CTRL-0078](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0078/) (Level 0): Enforce throttling or rate limits on agent-initiated database operations
- [CTRL-0082](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0082/) (Level 2): Do not grant agents access to personally identifiable or sensitive data unless strictly required
- [CTRL-0084](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0084/) (Level 0): Set minimum and maximum limits on what agents can modify within system resources
- [CTRL-0086](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0086/) (Level 0): Limit the number of concurrent queries to external systems by agents
- [CTRL-0089](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0089/) (Level 0): Enforce default-deny network egress for agent runtimes, allowing only approved destinations
- [CTRL-0097](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0097/) (Level 0): Do not give one agent untrusted content, access to sensitive data, and an unrestricted outbound channel at once; remove one, or gate the outbound channel outside the agent
- [CTRL-0098](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0098/) (Level 0): Keep credentials and backups out of reach of agent-run code
- [CTRL-0102](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0102/) (Level 1): Issue agents short-lived, task-scoped credentials, keep an inventory of them, and revoke them when an agent or integration is retired
- [CTRL-0104](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0104/) (Level 1): Authorise each action against the principal it is done for, at the agent that carries it out

## 2.2.1 · Clear allocation of responsibilities

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0002](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0002/) (Level 0): Obtain legally binding no-training and no-logging agreements from LLM API service providers
- [CTRL-0095](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0095/) (Level 1): Apply due diligence and technical bounds to third-party agents before delegating to them or transacting with them

## 2.2.2 · Design for meaningful human oversight

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0042](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0042/) (Level 1): Require explicit human confirmation before executing high-impact or irreversible tool actions
- [CTRL-0053](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0053/) (Level 0): Require human approval for communications on sensitive matters
- [CTRL-0056](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0056/) (Level 0): Require explicit human confirmation before committing any business transaction outside limits that an accountable human has pre-authorised
- [CTRL-0057](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0057/) (Level 2): Require out-of-band confirmation when transaction risk signals are elevated
- [CTRL-0070](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0070/) (Level 1): Review all agent-generated code before execution
- [CTRL-0076](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0076/) (Level 0): Require human approval for destructive changes to databases, tables, or files that cannot be readily undone
- [CTRL-0094](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0094/) (Level 0): Measure the quality of human oversight and redesign approval steps that have become rubber stamps
- [CTRL-0099](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0099/) (Level 1): Stop the task when an action is refused and report to a human, instead of letting the agent look for another route
- [CTRL-0101](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0101/) (Level 0): Give agents no write access to their own instructions, configuration, permissions, logs, or monitors
- [CTRL-0105](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0105/) (Level 1): Accept instructions and approvals only through a channel that proves they come from the principal

## 2.3.1 · Technical controls during design and development

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0001](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0001/) (Level 0): Use only LLMs from verified and trusted model developers
- [CTRL-0009](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0009/) (Level 0): Use only tool servers and APIs, including MCP servers, that implement robust authentication mechanisms in production environments
- [CTRL-0015](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0015/) (Level 1): Treat all tool metadata and outputs as untrusted input requiring validation
- [CTRL-0018](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0018/) (Level 2): Define default behaviour when the agent encounters ambiguous situations
- [CTRL-0019](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0019/) (Level 0): Keep untrusted inputs out of system instructions, and enclose any untrusted content given to the model in delimiters marked as data
- [CTRL-0020](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0020/) (Level 2): Use a dedicated LLM to extract required fields from inputs and filter out extraneous text or embedded instructions
- [CTRL-0021](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0021/) (Level 0): Implement allowlists and denylists to restrict what categories of information can be written to the agent's persistent memory
- [CTRL-0022](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0022/) (Level 1): Implement content filtering on writes to persistent memory to detect and block known unsafe content patterns
- [CTRL-0024](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0024/) (Level 0): Define formal schemas for inter-agent messages and validate all messages against these schemas before processing
- [CTRL-0025](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0025/) (Level 1): Ensure all inter-agent communications are encrypted in transit and prohibit plaintext channels
- [CTRL-0035](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0035/) (Level 2): Require agents to decompose user goals into explicit sub-goals and validate necessity before proceeding
- [CTRL-0039](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0039/) (Level 1): Ensure each agent publishes standardised, machine-readable capability descriptors accessible to other agents
- [CTRL-0041](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0041/) (Level 0): Provide comprehensive descriptions for each tool including intended use, required inputs, and potential outputs
- [CTRL-0044](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0044/) (Level 1): Implement output safety guardrails to detect and prevent generation of undesirable content
- [CTRL-0045](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0045/) (Level 1): Implement input guardrails to detect and decline requests for specialised domain advice
- [CTRL-0046](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0046/) (Level 1): Implement input guardrails to detect and decline requests for controversial content that violates organisational policies
- [CTRL-0047](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0047/) (Level 0): Implement output guardrails to detect and redact personally identifiable information
- [CTRL-0048](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0048/) (Level 2): Implement methods to reduce hallucination rates in agent outputs
- [CTRL-0051](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0051/) (Level 1): Implement input guardrails to detect and decline requests to generate copyrighted content
- [CTRL-0060](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0060/) (Level 1): Implement escape filtering before incorporating web content into prompts
- [CTRL-0062](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0062/) (Level 0): Implement input guardrails to detect prompt injection and adversarial attacks
- [CTRL-0063](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0063/) (Level 1): Prioritise search results from verified, high-quality domains
- [CTRL-0066](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0066/) (Level 0): Ensure "take over" mode is activated when entering sensitive data
- [CTRL-0067](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0067/) (Level 0): Ensure proper documentation of programmatic interfaces for agent use
- [CTRL-0068](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0068/) (Level 1): Use code linters to screen generated code for bad practices and poor syntax
- [CTRL-0071](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0071/) (Level 0): Use static code analysers to detect security vulnerabilities and code quality issues
- [CTRL-0074](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0074/) (Level 0): Conduct CVE scanning and block execution of code with High or Critical vulnerabilities
- [CTRL-0081](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0081/) (Level 1): Implement input guardrails to detect personally identifiable information in data accessed by agents
- [CTRL-0083](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0083/) (Level 0): Disallow unknown or external files unless they have been scanned for threats
- [CTRL-0090](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0090/) (Level 1): Enforce data-flow and capability policies at runtime with a deterministic policy layer that separates untrusted content from privileged actions
- [CTRL-0091](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0091/) (Level 0): Require verified provenance for tools, skills, and dependencies, and re-verify them on every update
- [CTRL-0096](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0096/) (Level 0): Harden agent frameworks and runtimes before exposing them, and patch framework vulnerabilities promptly
- [CTRL-0100](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0100/) (Level 0): Load instruction, settings, and tool-configuration files only from locations the operator controls, and ask before using any that arrive with a workspace
- [CTRL-0106](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0106/) (Level 1): Minimise the personal data an agent sends through its tools, and set a retention period for what it keeps

- [CTRL-0093](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0093/) (Level 2): Monitor agents for deceptive and collusive behaviour using an independent monitor
- [CTRL-0103](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0103/) (Level 1): Pin the model version, re-run evaluations before any model change, and keep a tested fallback

# Crosswalk: MITRE ATLAS

ARC maps its risks to [MITRE ATLAS (Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems)](https://atlas.mitre.org/) (2026.10 (28 October 2026)). Each mapping points to the nearest corresponding entry; it is not a claim that the two are the same.

Read it from either side: below, each item in that framework lists the ARC entries that map to it, and each ARC entry's own page lists its crosswalks.

# Crosswalk: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications

ARC maps its risks and controls to [OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026](https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/) (2026 (December 2025)). Each mapping points to the nearest corresponding entry; it is not a claim that the two are the same.

Read it from either side: below, each item in that framework lists the ARC entries that map to it, and each ARC entry's own page lists its crosswalks.

## ASI01 · Agent Goal Hijack

**Risks**

- [RISK-008](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-008/): Vague or underspecified instructions
- [RISK-009](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-009/): Unsanitised inputs in system instructions
- [RISK-019](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-019/): Generating plans that fail to meet the user's requirements
- [RISK-020](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-020/): Generating plans that overlook safety implications
- [RISK-032](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-032/): Unauthorised execution of business transactions
- [RISK-034](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-034/): Prompt injection via malicious websites
- [RISK-036](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-036/): Prompt injection risks through computer use
- [RISK-044](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-044/): Prompt injection via malicious files or data
- [RISK-047](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-047/): Data exfiltration through combined access to untrusted content, sensitive data, and an outbound channel
- [RISK-058](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-058/): Instruction and configuration files as a way in
- [RISK-059](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-059/): Prompt injection through inbound messages

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0016](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0016/) (Level 0): Define clearly the agent's role, scope, and non-goals in the system prompt
- [CTRL-0017](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0017/) (Level 1): Define clear success criteria for the agent's tasks
- [CTRL-0018](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0018/) (Level 2): Define default behaviour when the agent encounters ambiguous situations
- [CTRL-0019](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0019/) (Level 0): Keep untrusted inputs out of system instructions, and enclose any untrusted content given to the model in delimiters marked as data
- [CTRL-0020](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0020/) (Level 2): Use a dedicated LLM to extract required fields from inputs and filter out extraneous text or embedded instructions
- [CTRL-0035](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0035/) (Level 2): Require agents to decompose user goals into explicit sub-goals and validate necessity before proceeding
- [CTRL-0036](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0036/) (Level 1): Regularly evaluate and test planning behaviour under representative workloads and failure scenarios
- [CTRL-0037](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0037/) (Level 1): Require planning agents to include explicit safety constraints in all generated plans before execution
- [CTRL-0038](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0038/) (Level 0): Conduct safety verification with domain-relevant stress tests and adversarial scenarios before deployment and on a regular cadence afterwards
- [CTRL-0054](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0054/) (Level 1): Limit agent communications to standard processes with predefined templates
- [CTRL-0060](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0060/) (Level 1): Implement escape filtering before incorporating web content into prompts
- [CTRL-0061](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0061/) (Level 1): Use structured retrieval APIs for web searches rather than web scraping
- [CTRL-0062](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0062/) (Level 0): Implement input guardrails to detect prompt injection and adversarial attacks
- [CTRL-0083](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0083/) (Level 0): Disallow unknown or external files unless they have been scanned for threats
- [CTRL-0090](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0090/) (Level 1): Enforce data-flow and capability policies at runtime with a deterministic policy layer that separates untrusted content from privileged actions
- [CTRL-0097](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0097/) (Level 0): Do not give one agent untrusted content, access to sensitive data, and an unrestricted outbound channel at once; remove one, or gate the outbound channel outside the agent
- [CTRL-0100](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0100/) (Level 0): Load instruction, settings, and tool-configuration files only from locations the operator controls, and ask before using any that arrive with a workspace

## ASI02 · Tool Misuse and Exploitation

**Risks**

- [RISK-004](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-004/): Weak tool authentication and authorisation controls
- [RISK-006](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-006/): Tool poisoning by malicious actors
- [RISK-007](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-007/): Lack of input sanitisation
- [RISK-023](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-023/): Incorrect tool selection or misuse
- [RISK-032](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-032/): Unauthorised execution of business transactions
- [RISK-037](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-037/): Exposure of sensitive data
- [RISK-038](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-038/): Incorrect use of unfamiliar programmatic interfaces
- [RISK-041](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-041/): Unintended overwriting or deletion of files or data
- [RISK-042](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-042/): Database overload due to inefficient data operations
- [RISK-043](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-043/): Exposure of sensitive data through file or database access
- [RISK-045](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-045/): Misconfiguration of system resources
- [RISK-046](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-046/): System overload due to inefficient or excessive operations
- [RISK-047](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-047/): Data exfiltration through combined access to untrusted content, sensitive data, and an outbound channel
- [RISK-066](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-066/): Personal data collected, kept, or passed on beyond what the task needs

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0015](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0015/) (Level 1): Treat all tool metadata and outputs as untrusted input requiring validation
- [CTRL-0040](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0040/) (Level 0): Limit the scope of agent actions through predefined thresholds and baselines
- [CTRL-0041](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0041/) (Level 0): Provide comprehensive descriptions for each tool including intended use, required inputs, and potential outputs
- [CTRL-0042](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0042/) (Level 1): Require explicit human confirmation before executing high-impact or irreversible tool actions
- [CTRL-0043](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0043/) (Level 1): Log all tool selection decisions and invocations with comprehensive metadata
- [CTRL-0056](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0056/) (Level 0): Require explicit human confirmation before committing any business transaction outside limits that an accountable human has pre-authorised
- [CTRL-0059](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0059/) (Level 2): Apply fraud detection models or heuristics to agent-proposed transactions
- [CTRL-0064](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0064/) (Level 1): Limit computer use to accessing only safe and trusted resources
- [CTRL-0066](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0066/) (Level 0): Ensure "take over" mode is activated when entering sensitive data
- [CTRL-0067](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0067/) (Level 0): Ensure proper documentation of programmatic interfaces for agent use
- [CTRL-0072](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0072/) (Level 1): Monitor runtime and memory consumption of agent-generated code
- [CTRL-0075](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0075/) (Level 1): Do not grant write access to agents unless strictly necessary
- [CTRL-0076](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0076/) (Level 0): Require human approval for destructive changes to databases, tables, or files that cannot be readily undone
- [CTRL-0077](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0077/) (Level 0): Enable versioning or soft-delete for managed object stores to allow recovery from accidental modifications
- [CTRL-0078](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0078/) (Level 0): Enforce throttling or rate limits on agent-initiated database operations
- [CTRL-0079](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0079/) (Level 2): Validate agent-generated database queries for efficiency before execution against production databases
- [CTRL-0080](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0080/) (Level 2): Implement caching mechanisms to reduce repetitive database queries by agents
- [CTRL-0084](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0084/) (Level 0): Set minimum and maximum limits on what agents can modify within system resources
- [CTRL-0086](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0086/) (Level 0): Limit the number of concurrent queries to external systems by agents
- [CTRL-0089](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0089/) (Level 0): Enforce default-deny network egress for agent runtimes, allowing only approved destinations
- [CTRL-0097](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0097/) (Level 0): Do not give one agent untrusted content, access to sensitive data, and an unrestricted outbound channel at once; remove one, or gate the outbound channel outside the agent
- [CTRL-0106](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0106/) (Level 1): Minimise the personal data an agent sends through its tools, and set a retention period for what it keeps

## ASI03 · Identity and Privilege Abuse

**Risks**

- [RISK-004](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-004/): Weak tool authentication and authorisation controls
- [RISK-005](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-005/): Lack of proper role-based access control for tools
- [RISK-011](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-011/): Sensitive data leakage across memory contexts
- [RISK-015](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-015/): Overly permissive roles and permissions
- [RISK-016](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-016/): Unauthorised privilege escalation
- [RISK-021](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-021/): Incorrect task delegation between agents
- [RISK-022](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-022/): Malicious or manipulative use of delegated agents
- [RISK-033](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-033/): Leakage of transaction credentials
- [RISK-043](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-043/): Exposure of sensitive data through file or database access
- [RISK-049](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-049/): Escape from evaluation or sandbox containment onto live systems
- [RISK-054](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-054/): Insecure default configuration of agent frameworks and runtimes
- [RISK-056](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-056/): Actions beyond the agent's tools through code execution and reachable credentials
- [RISK-057](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-057/): Pursuit of a goal by means the principal did not sanction
- [RISK-060](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-060/): Agent credentials that are over-broad, long-lived, or outlive their use
- [RISK-063](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-063/): Authority passing between agents without a check
- [RISK-065](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-065/): Instructions or approvals forged in the principal's name

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0009](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0009/) (Level 0): Use only tool servers and APIs, including MCP servers, that implement robust authentication mechanisms in production environments
- [CTRL-0010](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0010/) (Level 1): Use only MCP servers that validate credentials on every inbound request
- [CTRL-0011](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0011/) (Level 0): Limit token scopes to the minimum privileges required and avoid broad or wildcard scopes
- [CTRL-0012](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0012/) (Level 2): Use only MCP servers that integrate with authorisation servers implementing per-client consent mechanisms
- [CTRL-0026](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0026/) (Level 1): Require all agents to authenticate with verifiable, cryptographically signed identities before processing requests
- [CTRL-0029](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0029/) (Level 0): Grant agents only the minimum permissions required for their designated tasks
- [CTRL-0030](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0030/) (Level 1): Assign each agent a unique, verifiable identity with no shared credentials
- [CTRL-0031](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0031/) (Level 1): Use only MCP servers that validate token provenance and prohibit unauthorised token passthrough
- [CTRL-0058](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0058/) (Level 0): Restrict agents to proposing transactions whilst using a separate transaction controller for execution
- [CTRL-0082](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0082/) (Level 2): Do not grant agents access to personally identifiable or sensitive data unless strictly required
- [CTRL-0096](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0096/) (Level 0): Harden agent frameworks and runtimes before exposing them, and patch framework vulnerabilities promptly
- [CTRL-0098](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0098/) (Level 0): Keep credentials and backups out of reach of agent-run code
- [CTRL-0101](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0101/) (Level 0): Give agents no write access to their own instructions, configuration, permissions, logs, or monitors
- [CTRL-0102](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0102/) (Level 1): Issue agents short-lived, task-scoped credentials, keep an inventory of them, and revoke them when an agent or integration is retired
- [CTRL-0104](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0104/) (Level 1): Authorise each action against the principal it is done for, at the agent that carries it out
- [CTRL-0105](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0105/) (Level 1): Accept instructions and approvals only through a channel that proves they come from the principal

## ASI04 · Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities

**Risks**

- [RISK-001](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-001/): Use of untrusted or compromised LLMs
- [RISK-006](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-006/): Tool poisoning by malicious actors
- [RISK-048](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-048/): Compromise through the tool, skill, and dependency supply chain
- [RISK-053](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-053/): Dependence on third-party agents as counterparties or delegates
- [RISK-058](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-058/): Instruction and configuration files as a way in
- [RISK-064](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-064/): Harm from a connected tool server or agent to the system that connects to it

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0001](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0001/) (Level 0): Use only LLMs from verified and trusted model developers
- [CTRL-0002](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0002/) (Level 0): Obtain legally binding no-training and no-logging agreements from LLM API service providers
- [CTRL-0003](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0003/) (Level 1): Use only established and verified model loaders in production environments
- [CTRL-0009](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0009/) (Level 0): Use only tool servers and APIs, including MCP servers, that implement robust authentication mechanisms in production environments
- [CTRL-0013](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0013/) (Level 0): Test all untested MCP servers in a sandboxed environment before deploying to production
- [CTRL-0015](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0015/) (Level 1): Treat all tool metadata and outputs as untrusted input requiring validation
- [CTRL-0074](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0074/) (Level 0): Conduct CVE scanning and block execution of code with High or Critical vulnerabilities
- [CTRL-0083](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0083/) (Level 0): Disallow unknown or external files unless they have been scanned for threats
- [CTRL-0091](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0091/) (Level 0): Require verified provenance for tools, skills, and dependencies, and re-verify them on every update
- [CTRL-0095](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0095/) (Level 1): Apply due diligence and technical bounds to third-party agents before delegating to them or transacting with them
- [CTRL-0100](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0100/) (Level 0): Load instruction, settings, and tool-configuration files only from locations the operator controls, and ask before using any that arrive with a workspace

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0003](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0003/) (Level 1): Use only established and verified model loaders in production environments
- [CTRL-0068](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0068/) (Level 1): Use code linters to screen generated code for bad practices and poor syntax

- [CTRL-0073](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0073/) (Level 0): Create a denylist of commands that agents are not permitted to execute

## ASI06 · Memory and Context Poisoning

**Risks**

- [RISK-010](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-010/): Poisoned memory
- [RISK-011](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-011/): Sensitive data leakage across memory contexts
- [RISK-027](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-027/): Regurgitating personally identifiable information
- [RISK-035](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-035/): Unreliable information or websites
- [RISK-044](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-044/): Prompt injection via malicious files or data

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0021](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0021/) (Level 0): Implement allowlists and denylists to restrict what categories of information can be written to the agent's persistent memory
- [CTRL-0022](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0022/) (Level 1): Implement content filtering on writes to persistent memory to detect and block known unsafe content patterns
- [CTRL-0023](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0023/) (Level 2): Log all modifications to persistent memory with comprehensive source metadata for audit purposes
- [CTRL-0063](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0063/) (Level 1): Prioritise search results from verified, high-quality domains

## ASI07 · Insecure Inter-Agent Communication

**Risks**

- [RISK-013](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-013/): Man-in-the-middle attacks between agents
- [RISK-051](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-051/): Unsanctioned coordination between agents
- [RISK-053](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-053/): Dependence on third-party agents as counterparties or delegates
- [RISK-063](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-063/): Authority passing between agents without a check
- [RISK-064](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/risk-064/): Harm from a connected tool server or agent to the system that connects to it

**Controls**

- [CTRL-0024](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0024/) (Level 0): Define formal schemas for inter-agent messages and validate all messages against these schemas before processing
- [CTRL-0025](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0025/) (Level 1): Ensure all inter-agent communications are encrypted in transit and prohibit plaintext channels
- [CTRL-0026](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0026/) (Level 1): Require all agents to authenticate with verifiable, cryptographically signed identities before processing requests
- [CTRL-0039](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0039/) (Level 1): Ensure each agent publishes standardised, machine-readable capability descriptors accessible to other agents
- [CTRL-0104](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0104/) (Level 1): Authorise each action against the principal it is done for, at the agent that carries it out

- [CTRL-0028](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0028/) (Level 0): Continuously monitor multi-agent systems for cascade failure indicators
- [CTRL-0032](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0032/) (Level 0): Centralise observability data collection in a unified backend system
- [CTRL-0033](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0033/) (Level 1): Standardise trace attributes for agent operations using consistent semantic conventions
- [CTRL-0034](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0034/) (Level 0): Conduct regular reviews of logs and traces to detect emergent issues in deployed agentic systems
- [CTRL-0040](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0040/) (Level 0): Limit the scope of agent actions through predefined thresholds and baselines
- [CTRL-0048](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0048/) (Level 2): Implement methods to reduce hallucination rates in agent outputs
- [CTRL-0085](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0085/) (Level 0): Log system health metrics and implement automated alerts for abnormal conditions
- [CTRL-0103](https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0103/) (Level 1): Pin the model version, re-run evaluations before any model change, and keep a tested fallback

# Crosswalk: OWASP agentic threats

ARC maps its risks to [OWASP Agentic AI – Threats and Mitigations (threat taxonomy, as reproduced in CSA Addendum Annex A)](https://genai.owasp.org/resource/agentic-ai-threats-and-mitigations/) (T1–T15 per CSA Addendum Annex A; T16–T17 per OWASP Top 10 Appendix A). Each mapping points to the nearest corresponding entry; it is not a claim that the two are the same.

Read it from either side: below, each item in that framework lists the ARC entries that map to it, and each ARC entry's own page lists its crosswalks.

# CTRL-0001 · Use only LLMs from verified and trusted model developers

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 0 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0001/

Untrusted or unknown model developers may introduce backdoors, data exfiltration risks, or inconsistent safety guarantees that compromise your agentic system. Establish evaluation criteria to assess model provider trustworthiness before adoption, including verification of published model cards, transparent responsible disclosure policies, evidence of security audits, and documented data handling practices. Evaluate whether the provider has an established track record, active security team, and clear incident response procedures. Regularly reassess providers against these criteria as new information emerges or the threat landscape evolves.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: organisation
- Owner: governance
- Phase: design, operate
- Evidence: The approved model provider register, with each provider's dated assessment against the trust criteria and the name of the assessor.
- Test: List every model endpoint the system calls in production and confirm each provider has a register entry assessed within the review period.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-001: Use of untrusted or compromised LLMs

## References

- https://www.csa.gov.sg/resources/publications/addendum-on-securing-ai-systems/
- https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/files/Guidelines-for-secure-AI-system-development.pdf
- https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm032025-supply-chain/

---

Source: https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0002/

# CTRL-0002 · Obtain legally binding no-training and no-logging agreements from LLM API service providers

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 0 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0002/

Without contractual protections, API providers may train models on your proprietary data or retain logs containing sensitive information, creating data leakage and compliance risks. Configure API settings to opt out of data logging and model training where available, and have your legal team review provider terms of service and data processing agreements to verify these protections are legally enforceable. Ensure alignment with your organisation's data governance and privacy requirements (e.g., GDPR, PDPA). Maintain records of these agreements and configurations for audit and compliance purposes.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: organisation, infrastructure
- Owner: governance
- Phase: design, deploy
- Evidence: The signed data processing agreement clause barring training on and retention of submitted data, and the provider account setting showing both switched off.
- Test: Open the provider console for the production API key and confirm training use and log retention are switched off, matching the contract clause.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-001: Use of untrusted or compromised LLMs

# CTRL-0003 · Use only established and verified model loaders in production environments

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0003/

Malicious or unvetted model loaders may execute arbitrary code during model deserialisation, potentially introducing backdoors or system vulnerabilities. Use well-maintained, community-vetted model loading libraries with active security support and regular updates. Examples include Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, or official framework loaders (PyTorch, TensorFlow), whilst avoiding custom or unmaintained deserialisation code. Monitor for security advisories affecting your chosen loaders and apply patches promptly.

## How to check it

- Owner: platform
- Phase: build, operate
- Evidence: The model-serving image's dependency lock file naming the loader library and pinned version, checked against the approved loader list.
- Test: Scan the production serving image and confirm it holds only an approved loader, at a version with no open security advisory, and no custom deserialisation code.

# CTRL-0004 · Review the LLM's system card to inform risk assessment and model selection

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 2 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0004/

System cards provide essential information about model capabilities, limitations, known failure modes, and safety evaluations that directly inform deployment decisions. Obtain and review the model's system card (or model card) before deployment, paying particular attention to documented risks, benchmark performance on safety evaluations, and limitations relevant to your use case. # CTRL-0005 · Conduct structured evaluation of multiple LLMs for instruction-following, performance, and safety before deployment

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0005/

Deploying an LLM without comparative evaluation risks selecting a model poorly suited to your use case, potentially resulting in safety issues, poor performance, or misaligned behaviour. Define evaluation criteria aligned with your application requirements (e.g., accuracy on domain-specific tasks, refusal of unsafe requests, consistency of outputs) and benchmark multiple candidate models against these criteria using representative test scenarios. Use both automated metrics and human evaluation to assess instruction-following quality, safety boundaries, and failure modes. Document evaluation results to support model selection decisions and establish baseline performance expectations for ongoing monitoring.

## How to check it

- Owner: developer
- Phase: design, build
- Evidence: The evaluation report scoring at least two candidate models on one test set for instruction-following, task performance and safety, with the selection decision.
- Test: Re-run the stored evaluation set against the deployed model version and confirm its scores fall within the tolerance recorded in the report.

# CTRL-0006 · Require human approval before executing high-impact actions

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0006/

Retired: replaced by CTRL-0042 (https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0042/).

Autonomous execution of high-impact actions without human oversight creates unacceptable risk of unintended consequences, including financial loss, data deletion, reputational damage, or safety incidents. Implement approval workflows that pause agent execution before critical actions (e.g., financial transactions, data deletion, external communications, system configuration changes) and present the proposed action with sufficient context for informed human decision-making. Design the approval interface to clearly display what will be executed, why the agent selected this action, and potential consequences. Ensure approval mechanisms cannot be bypassed by the agent and maintain audit logs of all approval decisions. Approval steps decay under volume: in one large deployment users approved about 93% of permission prompts. Pair this control with CTRL-0094 - measure approval and override rates, route routine actions to automated screening, and reserve human approval for genuinely uncertain or high-impact actions so that the approvals that remain are real decisions.

# CTRL-0007 · Log all LLM inputs and outputs for regular review

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 0 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0007/

# CTRL-0008 · Implement automated alerts when agent behaviour drifts from predefined thresholds

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0008/

Behavioural drift may indicate model degradation, adversarial manipulation, or emergent unsafe patterns that require immediate investigation. # CTRL-0009 · Use only tool servers and APIs, including MCP servers, that implement robust authentication mechanisms in production environments

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 0 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0009/

Weak or misconfigured authorisation on the servers and APIs that an agent's tools call can lead to unauthorised access, token theft, or privilege escalation that compromises connected systems. Before deployment, verify that every remote tool endpoint authenticates its caller with a standard mechanism (for example OAuth 2.1, OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, or mutually authenticated TLS) and enforces per-client scopes, and reject endpoints that rely on hard-coded credentials, unscoped shared keys, or deprecated authentication methods; test the authorisation flows in a development environment to confirm them. For MCP servers, also verify per-client consent flows and redirect URI validation to prevent authorisation bypasses, and reject servers with insufficient session management. As of the 2026-07-28 MCP specification, verify additionally that the server implements RFC 9207 issuer identification (so a client can detect a substituted authorization server) and Client ID Metadata Documents in place of dynamic client registration, and prefer servers that support the Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension so that access is governed by your identity provider rather than by per-user ad-hoc consent. Treat servers still built on the pre-2026 stateful session model as needing review before production use.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: infrastructure, organisation
- Owner: security
- Phase: build, deploy
- Evidence: The tool endpoint inventory recording each remote server's authentication mechanism and per-client scopes, with the integration review that exercised its authorisation flow.
- Test: Call each production tool endpoint with no credential and with a credential scoped for a different client, and confirm both are refused.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-004: Weak tool authentication and authorisation controls
- RISK-054: Insecure default configuration of agent frameworks and runtimes
- RISK-064: Harm from a connected tool server or agent to the system that connects to it

## References

- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/security_best_practices
- https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/

# CTRL-0010 · Use only MCP servers that validate credentials on every inbound request

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0010/

Relying on session state or connection-based authentication without per-request validation creates vulnerability to session hijacking, token replay attacks, and unauthorised access after initial authentication. Verify that MCP servers implement stateless authentication by validating credentials (e.g., OAuth tokens, API keys) on every single request rather than caching authorisation decisions based on connection or session state. Test this behaviour by monitoring whether the server accepts requests with expired, revoked, or missing credentials after an initial successful authentication. Ensure the server responds with appropriate HTTP 401 errors when credentials are invalid, expired, or absent, forcing re-authentication rather than relying on stale authorisation state. The 2026-07-28 specification removes long-lived stateful sessions from the protocol core, making per-request validation the expected behaviour; treat a server whose authorization depends on session state as non-compliant.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: infrastructure, organisation
- Owner: security
- Phase: build, deploy
- Evidence: The MCP server assessment record containing captured responses to requests sent with expired, revoked and missing tokens after an initial successful login.
- Test: Authenticate to the MCP server, revoke the token, send another request on the same connection and confirm it returns HTTP 401.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-064: Harm from a connected tool server or agent to the system that connects to it

## References

- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/security_best_practices
- https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/

# CTRL-0011 · Limit token scopes to the minimum privileges required and avoid broad or wildcard scopes

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 0 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0011/

Overly broad token scopes enable compromised or malicious actors to access resources beyond what is necessary for legitimate operations, amplifying the impact of security breaches. Define granular, task-specific scopes for each MCP server integration and request only the minimum permissions required for the intended functionality (e.g., "read:inventory" rather than "admin:*"). Review and document the justification for each requested scope during integration, and reject MCP servers that require unnecessarily broad permissions or fail to support fine-grained scope definitions. Periodically audit active token scopes to identify and revoke excessive permissions that may have accumulated over time.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: infrastructure, organisation
- Owner: developer
- Phase: build, operate
- Evidence: The OAuth client configuration listing each scope requested per tool integration with its justification, containing no wildcard or administrator scope.
- Test: Decode a token issued to the agent in production, confirm its scopes match the configured list, then call an out-of-scope operation and confirm refusal.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-005: Lack of proper role-based access control for tools
- RISK-060: Agent credentials that are over-broad, long-lived, or outlive their use

# CTRL-0012 · Use only MCP servers that integrate with authorisation servers implementing per-client consent mechanisms

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 2 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0012/

Without explicit per-client consent, a malicious or compromised client could abuse delegated permissions to access resources the user never intended to authorise for that specific application. Verify that MCP servers integrate with OAuth 2.1 authorisation servers that implement per-client consent flows, where users explicitly approve each client-permission combination rather than granting blanket permissions across all clients. The authorisation server should clearly identify the requesting client and display what data or actions are being requested during the consent flow. Ensure the authorisation server persists consent decisions and provides mechanisms for users to review and revoke previously granted permissions. With Client ID Metadata Documents (2026-07-28 specification), the authorization server identifies the client from its published metadata; check that consent screens name the client accurately, and use the Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension where a central identity provider should govern access on behalf of all users.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: infrastructure, organisation
- Owner: security
- Phase: build, deploy
- Evidence: A capture of the authorisation server's consent screen naming the client and the permissions requested, and of the page where users review and revoke grants.
- Test: Connect a second client under a user who has consented only to the first and confirm a fresh consent prompt appears before any access is granted.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-064: Harm from a connected tool server or agent to the system that connects to it

# CTRL-0015 · Treat all tool metadata and outputs as untrusted input requiring validation

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0015/

Tool metadata (descriptions, parameter names, schema definitions) can contain prompt injection attacks that manipulate agent behaviour even without tool invocation, whilst tool outputs may contain malicious content designed to compromise downstream systems. Validate and sanitise all tool metadata before exposing it to the LLM, treating tool descriptions with the same scrutiny as external user input and implementing content filtering to detect embedded instructions or adversarial prompts. Apply strict schema validation to tool outputs and sanitise responses before using them in prompts, displaying them to users, or passing them to other systems. Implement monitoring and logging of tool metadata and outputs to enable detection of injection attempts and post-incident analysis of compromised tool behaviour.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: harness, model
- Owner: developer
- Phase: build, operate
- Evidence: The tool-layer code that validates tool outputs against schemas and scans tool descriptions for embedded instructions, with its log of rejections.
- Test: Register a test tool whose description and output both carry an embedded instruction and confirm the description is flagged and the output rejected before reaching the model.

# CTRL-0016 · Define clearly the agent's role, scope, and non-goals in the system prompt

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 0 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0016/

Ambiguous or missing role definitions allow agents to interpret requests too broadly, potentially executing actions outside intended boundaries or misunderstanding their authority and constraints. Explicitly define the agent's purpose, permitted actions, and operational boundaries in the system prompt, including clear statements about what the agent should not do or attempt. Document specific examples of in-scope and out-of-scope behaviours to reduce ambiguity and guide the agent's decision-making in edge cases. # CTRL-0017 · Define clear success criteria for the agent's tasks

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0017/

Without explicit success criteria, agents may pursue task completion using inappropriate methods, over-optimise for partial objectives, or fail to recognise when they have achieved the intended outcome. Define measurable, verifiable success criteria for each task or category of tasks the agent performs, specifying both what constitutes successful completion and acceptable quality standards. Include criteria that address not just functional outcomes but also safety constraints, resource limits, and acceptable trade-offs. Regularly evaluate whether the agent's interpretation of success criteria aligns with intended outcomes and refine definitions to address observed gaps or misalignments.

- Owner: developer
- Phase: design, build
- Evidence: The task instructions in version control stating measurable completion and quality criteria per task type, with matching acceptance checks in the evaluation suite.
- Test: Run the acceptance checks on a sample of completed tasks and confirm the agent's own report of success agrees with the check result.

# CTRL-0018 · Define default behaviour when the agent encounters ambiguous situations

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 2 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0018/

Agents encountering ambiguous instructions without clear fallback behaviour may make incorrect assumptions, proceed with risky actions, or halt unexpectedly, reducing reliability and increasing safety risks. Establish a default policy for handling ambiguity that aligns with your risk tolerance, such as requesting human clarification, selecting the most conservative option, or declining to act until uncertainty is resolved. Document this policy in the system prompt and provide examples of ambiguous scenarios to guide agent decision-making. Monitor how often the agent invokes ambiguity handling mechanisms to identify areas where task definitions or instructions require clarification.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: prompt
- Owner: developer
- Phase: design, build, operate
- Evidence: The system prompt section stating the default action under ambiguity with worked examples, and a dashboard counting how often the agent invokes it.
- Test: Give the agent an instruction with two conflicting readings and confirm it takes the stated default, such as asking for clarification, before any tool call.

## Risks it addresses

# CTRL-0019 · Keep untrusted inputs out of system instructions, and enclose any untrusted content given to the model in delimiters marked as data

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 0 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0019/

Prompt injection attacks exploit LLMs' inability to distinguish between instructions and data, allowing malicious users to embed commands within input that override intended behaviour. Do not interpolate user input, retrieved content, or tool outputs into the system prompt or other instruction templates; fix the system prompt at build time and pass untrusted content to the model in the user or tool turns, where it carries less authority. Where untrusted content must be quoted, enclose it within clearly marked boundaries (e.g., XML tags or special markers) that are unlikely to appear naturally in the input, and instruct the LLM to treat delimited content as data rather than instructions. Neither measure is a complete defence, because the model can still follow instructions in untrusted content, so combine them with controls that do not depend on the model's compliance, such as a deterministic policy layer (CTRL-0090) and least privilege (CTRL-0029).

## How to check it

- Enforcement: harness, prompt
- Owner: developer
- Phase: build
- Evidence: The prompt-assembly code showing a fixed system prompt with no interpolated variables and a wrapper that places untrusted content inside tagged data blocks.
- Test: Submit input containing the closing delimiter followed by an instruction and confirm the logged system prompt is unchanged and the input sits escaped inside its data block.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-009: Unsanitised inputs in system instructions
- RISK-058: Instruction and configuration files as a way in
- RISK-059: Prompt injection through inbound messages

## References

- https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/blog-post/prompt-injection-is-not-sql-injection
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.14720
- https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/LLM_Prompt_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html

# CTRL-0020 · Use a dedicated LLM to extract required fields from inputs and filter out extraneous text or embedded instructions

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 2 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0020/

Using the same LLM for both input processing and task execution creates vulnerability to prompt injection attacks embedded in user input. Deploy a separate LLM instance configured specifically for input sanitisation, with explicit instructions to extract only designated fields (e.g., name, email, query text) whilst ignoring any other content including embedded commands or meta-instructions. Configure this extraction LLM with a restrictive system prompt focused solely on structured data extraction and validation against expected schemas. Validate extracted fields against expected formats before passing them to the main agent LLM, and monitor extraction outputs for anomalies that might indicate injection attempts.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: model, harness
- Owner: developer
- Phase: design, build
- Evidence: The pipeline configuration showing a separate extraction model call, with its own restrictive prompt and output schema, placed before the main agent.
- Test: Submit an input with an instruction appended to a form field and confirm only schema-valid field values appear in the main agent's logged context.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-009: Unsanitised inputs in system instructions

# CTRL-0021 · Implement allowlists and denylists to restrict what categories of information can be written to the agent's persistent memory

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 0 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0021/

Unrestricted writes to persistent memory enable attackers to poison agent memory with malicious instructions, false information, or sensitive data that could compromise future agent behaviour or leak confidential information. Define explicit allowlists of permitted memory categories (e.g., user preferences, conversation context, task history) and denylists of forbidden content (e.g., credentials, system instructions, security policies, prompt overrides). Enforce these restrictions at the memory write interface, validating all write operations against the defined policies before persisting data.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: harness
- Owner: developer
- Phase: build, operate
- Evidence: The memory-write policy file listing permitted and forbidden content categories, and the write-interface code that checks every write against it.
- Test: Ask the agent to remember an API key and a new standing instruction and confirm both writes are refused and logged.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-010: Poisoned memory
- RISK-011: Sensitive data leakage across memory contexts

# CTRL-0022 · Implement content filtering on writes to persistent memory to detect and block known unsafe content patterns

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0022/

Malicious actors may attempt to inject adversarial content into agent memory that bypasses category-based restrictions, such as jailbreak prompts, command injection templates, or social engineering content designed to manipulate future agent behaviour. Deploy content filtering mechanisms that scan all memory write operations for known unsafe patterns (e.g., jailbreak strings, tool invocation templates, prompt override attempts, phishing content) before persisting data. Implement filtering using prompt injection detectors (to detect jailbreak strings) or custom classifiers finetuned on specific risks (e.g. attempts to invoke tools maliciously).

- Phase: build, operate
- Evidence: The memory-write filter configuration naming the injection detector or classifier and its threshold, with the log of blocked writes.
- Test: Attempt to store a known jailbreak string and a tool-invocation template in memory and confirm the filter blocks both before they persist.

# CTRL-0023 · Log all modifications to persistent memory with comprehensive source metadata for audit purposes

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 2 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0023/

Without detailed audit logs, detecting and investigating memory poisoning attacks becomes extremely difficult, preventing effective incident response and forensic analysis. Implement comprehensive logging for all memory write, update, and delete operations, capturing source metadata including timestamps, user or agent identity, session context, and the specific content being modified. Structure logs to enable correlation analysis, allowing security teams to trace how specific memory entries evolved over time and identify suspicious modification patterns. Store audit logs in a tamper-evident system separate from the agent's operational memory to prevent attackers from covering their tracks by deleting or modifying log entries.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: harness, infrastructure
- Owner: developer
- Phase: build, operate
- Evidence: A memory audit log query for one entry returning every write, update and delete with timestamp, actor identity, session and changed content.
- Test: Create, edit and delete a memory entry and confirm three matching audit records exist in a store the agent's credentials cannot modify.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-010: Poisoned memory
- RISK-011: Sensitive data leakage across memory contexts

# CTRL-0024 · Define formal schemas for inter-agent messages and validate all messages against these schemas before processing

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 0 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0024/

Unstructured or inadequately validated inter-agent messages create vulnerability to injection attacks, misinterpretation, and parsing errors that could compromise agent behaviour or cascade through multi-agent systems. Define explicit message schemas using formal specification languages (e.g., JSON Schema, Protobuf, OpenAPI) that specify required fields, data types, validation rules, and permitted value ranges for all agent-to-agent communications. Implement strict input validation that verifies all incoming messages conform to expected schemas, checking field presence, data types, value ranges, and structural integrity before processing message content. Reject messages that are incomplete, contain unexpected fields, violate type constraints, or include suspicious patterns, returning explicit error responses to the sending agent and logging validation failures to enable detection of compromised or malfunctioning agents.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: harness
- Owner: developer
- Phase: design, build
- Evidence: The inter-agent message schemas in version control and the validator invoked at each agent's message entry point.
- Test: Send an agent a message with a missing required field and an undeclared extra field and confirm it returns an error and logs a validation failure.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-012: Cascading errors in multi-agent architectures
- RISK-022: Malicious or manipulative use of delegated agents
- RISK-051: Unsanctioned coordination between agents
- RISK-053: Dependence on third-party agents as counterparties or delegates
- RISK-063: Authority passing between agents without a check

# CTRL-0025 · Ensure all inter-agent communications are encrypted in transit and prohibit plaintext channels

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0025/

Unencrypted inter-agent communications expose sensitive data, credentials, and operational context to network-based attackers through eavesdropping or man-in-the-middle attacks. Ensure all agent-to-agent network communications use transport-layer encryption (minimum TLS 1.2, preferably TLS 1.3), including internal traffic within trusted network boundaries, as internal networks are increasingly targeted by sophisticated attackers. For protocol-based frameworks (e.g., A2A Protocol), verify that TLS is enabled by default; for application frameworks (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI), configure deployment infrastructure to enforce HTTPS endpoints for all remote agent APIs. Configure agents to reject plaintext connections and verify certificates to prevent downgrade attacks or rogue agent impersonation, and regularly audit network traffic to detect agents attempting unencrypted communication.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: infrastructure
- Owner: platform
- Phase: build, deploy
- Evidence: The service mesh or load balancer configuration requiring TLS 1.2 or higher on every agent endpoint, with plaintext listeners disabled.
- Test: Attempt a plaintext HTTP connection and a TLS 1.0 handshake to each agent endpoint and confirm both are refused.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-012: Cascading errors in multi-agent architectures
- RISK-022: Malicious or manipulative use of delegated agents
- RISK-053: Dependence on third-party agents as counterparties or delegates

## References

- https://a2aprotocol.ai/blog/2025-full-guide-a2a-protocol

# CTRL-0026 · Require all agents to authenticate with verifiable, cryptographically signed identities before processing requests

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0026/

Without strong agent authentication, attackers can impersonate legitimate agents to gain unauthorised access, inject malicious commands, or exfiltrate sensitive data from multi-agent systems. Implement cryptographic identity verification using mechanisms such as mutual TLS (mTLS), signed JWTs, or certificate-based authentication to ensure each agent presents verifiable credentials before processing its requests. Configure the authentication system to validate that credentials are properly signed by a trusted authority, have not expired, and belong to the claimed agent identity. Reject unauthenticated requests immediately and log authentication failures to detect potential impersonation attempts or compromised agents attempting to bypass security controls. Both the A2A Protocol and LangGraph provide native support for cryptographic agent authentication through mTLS, OAuth 2.0, and JWT-based identity verification.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: infrastructure, harness
- Owner: platform
- Phase: build, deploy
- Evidence: The mutual TLS or token-validation configuration on each agent endpoint naming the trusted issuer, with authentication failures visible in the log.
- Test: Send an agent requests carrying no credential, an expired token and a certificate from an untrusted authority, and confirm all three are rejected and logged.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-013: Man-in-the-middle attacks between agents
- RISK-051: Unsanctioned coordination between agents
- RISK-053: Dependence on third-party agents as counterparties or delegates
- RISK-063: Authority passing between agents without a check

# CTRL-0027 · Implement circuit breakers to prevent cascading failures in multi-agent systems

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0027/

Without circuit breakers, failures in one agent can cascade through multi-agent systems, causing widespread outages, resource exhaustion, or degraded performance across interconnected agents. Implement circuit breaker patterns that monitor agent interactions and automatically halt requests to failing agents when error rates, timeouts, or response times exceed predefined thresholds. Configure circuit breakers with appropriate timeout values, retry limits, and failure thresholds based on your system's tolerance for latency and error rates.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: harness
- Owner: developer
- Phase: build, operate
- Evidence: The circuit-breaker settings in the orchestration configuration giving failure threshold, timeout and retry limit for each agent-to-agent call.
- Test: Make one downstream agent return errors continuously and confirm callers stop sending it requests once the threshold is reached.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-012: Cascading errors in multi-agent architectures

# CTRL-0028 · Continuously monitor multi-agent systems for cascade failure indicators

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 0 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0028/

Cascade failures can rapidly propagate through multi-agent systems, but early detection enables intervention before widespread system degradation occurs. Implement monitoring that tracks indicators of cascading failures including agent looping behaviour, repeated error patterns, diverging outputs across similar agents, and abnormal request rates between agents. Configure alerting thresholds that trigger when cascade indicators exceed acceptable levels, such as the same agent repeatedly calling the same endpoint, multiple agents simultaneously failing similar requests, or circular dependencies in agent communication patterns.

- Owner: developer
- Phase: deploy, operate
- Evidence: The dashboards and alert rules covering inter-agent request rates, repeated identical calls, simultaneous failures and circular call chains.
- Test: Set two agents calling each other in a loop in staging and confirm an alert naming both fires within the configured window.

# CTRL-0029 · Grant agents only the minimum permissions required for their designated tasks

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 0 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0029/

Excessive permissions enable compromised or malfunctioning agents to access sensitive resources, modify critical data, or perform actions beyond their intended scope, amplifying the impact of security breaches. Apply the principle of least privilege by defining granular permission sets for each agent based on its specific role and required operations, avoiding blanket administrative access or broad permission grants. Review agent permissions regularly to ensure they remain aligned with current responsibilities, revoking unnecessary access as agent roles evolve.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: infrastructure, harness
- Owner: developer
- Phase: design, build, operate
- Evidence: Each agent's IAM policy and tool permission manifest, with every permission tied to a named task, and the latest access review record.
- Test: Using the agent's credentials, attempt an operation outside its role, such as reading another system's data store, and confirm it is denied.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-014: Feedback loops and runaway agent behaviour
- RISK-015: Overly permissive roles and permissions
- RISK-016: Unauthorised privilege escalation
- RISK-049: Escape from evaluation or sandbox containment onto live systems
- RISK-056: Actions beyond the agent's tools through code execution and reachable credentials
- RISK-057: Pursuit of a goal by means the principal did not sanction
- RISK-060: Agent credentials that are over-broad, long-lived, or outlive their use
- RISK-063: Authority passing between agents without a check

# CTRL-0030 · Assign each agent a unique, verifiable identity with no shared credentials

ARC risk register 2.0.0-draft.1, Level 1 control. https://govtech-responsibleai.github.io/arc-v2-draft/register/ctrl-0030/

Shared credentials prevent accurate attribution of agent actions, making it impossible to identify which agent performed unauthorised activities or to revoke access for compromised agents without affecting legitimate ones. Assign each agent instance a unique identity (e.g., service account, API key, certificate) that can be independently tracked, audited, and revoked without impacting other agents. Prohibit credential sharing between agents even when they perform similar functions, as unique identities enable granular access control and forensic analysis of agent behaviour. Emerging agentic IAM platforms, such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, can help to provide purpose-built identity management for AI agents. Concrete mechanisms now exist: SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identities with short rotation for agents and MCP servers, Microsoft Entra Agent ID (assigned to all new Copilot Studio agents since July 2026), and the IETF drafts for OAuth on-behalf-of delegation and transaction tokens that carry separate actor (agent) and principal (initiating human) claims; A2A v1.0 signed agent cards provide the equivalent for agent-to-agent interactions. Prefer identities that keep the delegating human visible in every token so that actions remain attributable.

## How to check it

- Enforcement: infrastructure
- Owner: platform
- Phase: build, operate, retire
- Evidence: The identity provider's list of agent service accounts or workload identities, showing one per agent instance and no key shared between two.
- Test: Revoke one agent's credential and confirm only that agent loses access, and that the audit log attributes its earlier actions to it alone.

## Risks it addresses

- RISK-015: Overly permissive roles and permissions
- RISK-016: Unauthorised privilege escalation
- RISK-060: Agent credentials that are over-broad, long-lived, or outlive their use

## References

- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/identity-overview.html
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/agent-id-governance-overview
- https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-oauth-transaction-tokens-for-agents-04
- https://www.hashicorp.com/en/blog/spiffe-securing-the-identity-of-agentic-ai-and-non-human-actors
